title: S022 — Unfounded-set candidate boundary / incremental cycle observability
description: Characterise the global Phase-B (unfounded-set) boundary: is it inherently global, conditionally global, reducible to a smaller candidate frontier, or amenable to compact maintained state?
result_summary: HOLD. The Phase-B candidate set is EXACTLY the NEITHER set after Phase A. Measured on both seed canons: |C| (candidates) = 0.07-1.31 nodes and dC = 0.00-0.19 (LOCAL); |U| (unfounded) = 0.00 and dU = 0.00 (EMPTY). So Phase B is GLOBAL SCAN + EMPTY/LOCAL RESULT, and its scan domain is itself tiny - the global barrier is a cheap consistency pass over a handful of nodes, not a whole-model sweep. Relationship: support aggregate change -> NEITHER-set change (= dC) -> Phase B re-scan; no separate trigger observed. External-support sensitivity is the shrink rule itself. Observation only: observeUnfoundedSet reads the authoritative unfoundedSet; no reimplementation. HOLD because the |U|>0 case (constructed cycles) was NOT tested - the seed canons have no unfounded nodes.

answers.Q1_candidate_set: exactly the NEITHER set after Phase A (the unfoundedSet scan domain)
answers.Q2_candidate_membership_change: when Phase A changes the NEITHER set (the semantic delta's NEITHER component)
answers.Q4_dU_local: YES - 0.00 on the seed canons (empty unfounded set)
answers.Q5_why_global: implementation, not semantics - the scan is global by construction but its domain (NEITHER nodes) is small
answers.Q6_scc_sufficient: not tested; the implementation trigger is external-support membership, i.e. dC
answers.Q7_support_triggers_phase_b: YES - a support change can alter the NEITHER set with no topology change
answers.Q8_external_support_local: localised to the affected candidate's groups; not tested on constructed cycles
answers.Q9_boundary_exists: a principled boundary exists (the NEITHER set / dC); general sufficiency requires the cycle corpus
answers.Q10_future_state: the NEITHER-set membership (candidate set) and its cross-prefix delta, plus SCC membership for real cycles
answers.Q11_global_barrier_ok: YES - Phase B can remain a global barrier since its domain is small and cheap to rescan

next_experiment: exercise the |U|>0 path with constructed cycles (bootstrap, overlapping, external-support gain/loss, cycle cascade) to test whether dC suffices to predict Phase-B reconsideration.
limitations: No constructed cycles: the seed canons have |U|=0, so the path where Phase B actually rejects nodes was not tested.
No cycle-free control, SCC matrix, external-support sensitivity, or cascade test (budget).
No long-horizon, determinism, or branch measurements.
